items.title: Presentation to Jeff Hoffman from the Grove Hubs by Mayor Watters
notes: Mayor Watters presented Jeff Hoffman from the Grove Hubs with a cheque in the amount of $24,000, the proceeds from the 1st annual Mayor’s golf tournament.
Jeff Hoffman provided an overview of the youth wellness programs offered, including services related to mental health, finding employment or housing for youth.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters provided highlights from the County Warden’s Inaugural meeting held on December 6th with Chris White elected as the new Warden.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Members of Council provided updates on the various activities of the advisory committees and highlights of exciting upcoming local events.

items.title: Consent Items
notes: Mayor Watters indicated Consent Agenda Items are considered routine in nature and are voted on collectively. Any Member of Council may request one or more items be removed from the Consent Agenda for separate action.

With respect to item 10.3 regarding the contaminant discharge to the storm sewer in Belwood, Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services responded to questions regarding the source of the contamination and the communication measures taken by staff and the Ministry of the Environment.

items.title: Approval and Receipt of Minutes
notes: THAT the minutes of the Council Meeting held November 25, 2024 and Budget Committee of the Whole held December 3, 2024 be approved as circulated;
AND the Heritage Centre Wellington minutes be received for information.
THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the report from the Committee of the Whole dated December 3, 2024 as follows:

1. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington endorses and directs staff to submit an application for grant funding from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) – Municipal Fleet Electrification Fund;
AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington receives for information the updated “Class C” construction cost estimate for construction of the new Township Operations Centre.
2. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington authorize the Mayor and Clerk to sign a By-Law to endorse a new Fleet Policy for the Township of Centre Wellington.
AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington direct staff to enact and adhere to the Fleet Policy effective December 31, 2024.

3. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington pass a by-law to establish the 2025 fees and charges for various services provided by the Township, and repeal by-laws 2023-95, 2024-29, and 2024-45.
4. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the 2025 Business Plan as amended.

5. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington adopt Report No. COR2024-71 regarding additional financial disclosure requirements for the 2025 budget year pursuant to Ontario Regulation 284/09.
6. THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approve the 2025 Budget.

items.title: By-law to Restrict the Weight of Vehicles Passing Over Certain Bridges
notes: in the Township of Centre Wellington

Report from A. Dickieson, Engineering Services Coordinator Adam Dickieson, Engineering Services Coordinator provided an overview of the report, including recommendations to apply load restrictions to specific bridges.

He responded to questions regarding the impact on the farmers and emergency services response times and the urgency to expedite the replacement of bridge 29-WG. He also commented on the support of the OPP to enforce the weight restrictions.

items.title: Development Charge Deferral Agreement - Jefferson Elora Corporation
notes: Report from G. Borovilos, Manager of Economic Development George Borovilos, Manager of Economic Development provided an overview of the report, indicating Jefferson Elora is planning a building expansion to their stamping department and has requested a deferral of development charges to assist with the company’s financial obligation during the construction period.

items.title: Short Term Rental Licensing By-law Update
notes: Report from K. O’Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk
Kerri O’Kane, Manager of Legislative Services & Municipal Clerk provided an overview of the report and responded to questions.

Members of Council provided comments on a requirement for all Short Term Rental’s (STRs) provide a parking plan and no grandfathering of existing STRs within the commercial core, consideration to limit the number of bedrooms permitted to prevent party houses and limiting STRs to principle residences or hosted rather than un-hosted and use of the urban boundary area as a template rather than the heritage overlay.
